correctness.rationale: For uniform period arrival, integrate every active gap to obtain W=(T/2)E sum_J(sum_{i in J}g_i)^2. A Hessian H is strictly positive definite as all buses run with probability product_i p_i>0. Forward/backward first-active recurrences have finite unique cyclic solutions because a guaranteed departure has zero failure probability. Substitution of g_i*=(v_i+v_{i+1})/(2S) and q_i=(1-v_i)/(1+v_i) yields A_i=B_i=(1+v_i)/(2S), hence Hg*=1/S; strict convexity establishes unique global optimality, W*=T/(2S), order invariance, and the exact squared-block regret identity. Independent standard-library exact-rational checker passed 21 complete enumeration configurations with 12 distinct reliability permutations; finite checks do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: Scheduling under heterogeneous independent missed runs, a standard reliability issue, lacks a simple all-count exact policy in the inspected motivating literature. The theorem provides a complete and operationally interpretable solution for every n>=4 and every admissible reliability vector, proves that the minimal expected wait is independent of cyclic reliability order despite different optimal gaps, and gives an exact strict regret measure; the four-service example shows a nontrivial 47/407 wait reduction relative to equal headways. It is not just a renamed three-detector fact, a fixed-parameter numerical exercise, or a universal statement about realistic transit systems.
